title: Pashpasha
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In the Jerusalem Talmud, Shevi'it ch. 6, halakha 1: "Pashpasha. Rabbi Yose said: I asked Rabbi Abba." And [the commentary] Penei Moshe explains that it is the name of a sage, but it seems more likely that it is the name of a place.
Ahavat Tziyon explains pashpasha instead as an expression of the need for examination, comparing Ketubot 110b: “A pleasant dwelling puts a person to the test.”

notes.text: Penei Moshe takes Pashpasha as a sage; Hyman prefers a place-name; Ahavat Tziyon gives a verbal explanation. Ketubot 110b explains bodily testing in terms of illness caused by a change of habit, not a dwelling literally inspecting something.
The consulted Penei Moshe calls Pashpasha the name of a man and says he asked Rabbi Acha. Hyman’s quoted text names Rabbi Abba.
